other_conflicting_accesses: The same four lines exist in dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu kernel10 at L1194-1195 (stores), L1201 (atomicInc), L1214-1215 (loads); in kernels 9 (atomicInc L1001, loads L1014-1015), 8 (atomicInc L843), 7 (atomicAdd L731), 6 (atomicAdd L638) of the same file the hand-off is the same (the record lists flag atomics at L638, L731, L843, L1001, L1201; loads/stores of kernels 6-8 were not individually read). Whether T21b/T21c builds the dev/cuda file or llmc/layernorm.cuh determines which file/lines the SASS attribution will point to.

The hand-off flag itself, `*tmp_flag = atomicInc(scratchFlag, gridDim.x);` at llmc/layernorm.cuh L378 (thread 0, relaxed atom.global.inc on scratch[0], a different address from the partials), is an atomic and not part of the racing pair; it is the attempted publication.
thread_pair_example: dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu kernel10 (llmc/layernorm.cuh line in brackets): block A thread t stores 128 bits at scratch_dbias + i + 2*C*A (L1194 [L371], i = t*4) after __syncthreads L1183 [L360] and before __syncthreads L1197 [L374]; its thread 0 then does atomicInc on scratchFlag (L1201 [L378]). The last-arriving block B (atomicInc returned gridDim.x - 1) passes __syncthreads L1203 [L380] and thread t loads the same address at L1214 [L391] (read_block_idx = A). No __threadfence on either side; bar.sync is CTA-scope and the relaxed atomic on another address releases nothing.
class_reason: Both accesses are plain (non-volatile, non-atomic) 128-bit global accesses (verify.strong_accesses: none for the pair); the atomicInc flag is the attempted hand-off only (relaxed, different address). bar.sync orders threads within one CTA only and a relaxed atomic on another address does not release the earlier stores, so there is no happens-before edge from block A's stores to the last block's loads. Plain vs plain unordered = DR under D20. In practice it works because L2 atomics execute after earlier stores of the same SM drain; formally it is message passing without release/acquire.
buggy_expected: the pair (dev/cuda/layernorm_backward.cu L1194/L1195 store128 by block A) x (L1214/L1215 load128 by the last block) on global scratch is reported as DR (cross-block RAW); if the production header is built instead, the same pair is llmc/layernorm.cuh L371/L372 x L391/L392 (sites_llmc_layernorm_cuh). A detector must model atomicInc as relaxed and must not treat bar.sync or any atomic as a GPU-scope fence

upstream_status.dispute_points: (1) On real hardware this essentially always works because atomics execute at L2 after earlier stores from the same SM have drained; a skeptic will say 'not observable'. The detector follows PTX happens-before, under which it IS a race (message-passing without release/acquire), and the author's own earlier kernel5 includes the fence. (2) The detector must model atomicInc as relaxed (not acq_rel) and not treat the CTA-level __syncthreads as a GPU-scope fence; if it treats any atomic as a full fence it will miss this. (3) Repo is archived-ish (last commit 2025-05), so no fix is expected.
